# Review CHANGES REQUESTED for PAN-4598

# Review — PAN-4598
## Verdict: CHANGES REQUESTED — the unaddressed plan critique leaves two FR-4 violations: Retry promises a batch it will not build, and the failure time shown is the cleanup time

## Context
- Run ID: agent-pan-4598-review-41f0947f
- Manifest: /home/eltmon/Projects/overdeck/workspaces/feature-pan-4598/.pan/review/agent-pan-4598-review-41f0947f/context.json
- Branch / workspace: feature/pan-4598 · /home/eltmon/Projects/overdeck/workspaces/feature-pan-4598
- PR: #4603
- HEAD reviewed: 41f0947f02697aeb40ce449e03fcb26630682412
- Base / prior cycle SHA: merge-base 5341601b111 (origin/main); no prior review cycle

The fix commit 3325ab5af5e (05:12) came before `.pan/drafts/pan-4598-critique.md`, which was committed in bfb47e37297 (06:51). The critique has three `blocks-the-design` items. No code commit after it addresses any of them, and the PR body does not defer them to a follow-up. I re-checked all three against HEAD, and all three are still live. Two of them break the explicit text of FR-4.

## Blocking Findings

### [requirements] Retry batch assembly promises a batch for a lone unheld feature — `src/dashboard/frontend/src/components/merge-train/MergeTrainView.tsx:694`
- Severity: !
- Classification / requirement scope: implementation defect; in_pr_scope (FR-4: "The card never promises a batch it will not build.")
- Trigger and changed-code connection: the Retry button renders when `lastAssemblyFailed && featureCount > 0` (line 694). Its confirm (`retryAssemblyConfirmCopy`, `mergeTrainCopy.ts:54`) says "This builds a new test batch from <project>'s 1 ready feature". The forced reconcile it posts (`postMergeTrainAssemblePayload` → `runUatTrainReconcile({ force: true })`) still returns `single-feature` before assembly when one unheld feature is ready (`uat-reconciler.ts`, the `readySet.length < MIN_BATCH_FEATURES && !holdsForUat` branch). The code comment there says "force does not override this".
- Expected / observed / impact: here is a reachable path. In a project that does not hold for UAT, a two-feature batch fails. The operator then merges one feature with the new row **Merge** button. The reconciler returns `single-feature` and writes no new row, so the newest generation stays `failed`. The section line then shows `SINGLE_FEATURE_READY_LINE` ("merges directly"), and right below it the card offers **Retry batch assembly**, whose confirm promises a new test batch. Clicking it builds nothing, and a toast then says "merges directly". The card contradicts itself, and the confirm promises a batch it cannot build. That is the exact sentence FR-4 forbids. The PR's own row-Merge flow makes this state routine.
- Evidence: static trace of line 694, `mergeTrainCopy.ts:51-57`, the reconciler single-feature branch, and `rebuildMutation.onSuccess` (the `single-feature` toast). No test covers this case. The critique asked for "a failed two-feature attempt followed by one unheld ready feature".
- Fix: render Retry only when the current ready set can form a batch: `featureCount >= 2 || section.holdsForUat !== false`. For a single-row queue, `holdsForUat` is already that issue's effective hold. Add the view test the critique named.

### [requirements] The card's failure time and the cutoff's age read a timestamp that cleanup overwrites — `src/dashboard/frontend/src/components/merge-train/mergeTrainCopy.ts:15` and `src/lib/cloister/uat-reconciler.ts:313`
- Severity: !
- Classification / requirement scope: implementation defect; in_pr_scope. FR-4 says the card "names the failure and its time". FR-1 says a failed generation older than 6 hours does not count.
- Trigger and changed-code connection: `formatFailedAt` and the new streak loop both read `gen.updatedAt || gen.createdAt`. `cleanupUatGenerations` (`uat-generation-engine.ts`, about line 484) writes `cleanedAt` on failed rows. `updateUatGeneration` (`merge-sync-uat.ts`, about lines 467-474) sets `updated_at = nowMillis()` on every scalar update. So `updatedAt` on a failed row is the cleanup time, not the failure time.
- Expected / observed / impact: I read the live database read-only (`~/.overdeck/overdeck.db`, table `uat_generations`). The three rows this issue is about read like this:
  - `uat/pan-onyx-0920-4`: created 16:12:22, `updated_at` 19:14:24
  - `uat/pan-onyx-0920-5`: created 17:13:22, `updated_at` 19:14:24
  - `uat/pan-onyx-0920-6`: created 18:13:32, `updated_at` 19:14:23

  All three rows carry the cleanup time. After deploy, the card will say `pan-onyx-0920-6` "failed at Sep 20, 19:14", which is about an hour after that assembly actually died. The same drift moves the 6-hour window forward by the cleanup delay. Here that delay was 1-3 hours. When cleanup runs in the same tick, the delay is only seconds. The test fixture `PAN_FAILED_GEN` copies this real gap (createdAt 18:13, updatedAt 19:14) and asserts no time. The critique raised this point and asked for a test of a failed row that is cleaned up later.
- Evidence: static trace of the store update path, plus the live rows above. Limits: the live rows are weeks old, so they expire correctly either way, and the permanent latch is fixed. The defect is the stated failure time and the length of the window.
- Fix: the simplest fix is for both readers to use `createdAt`. That is immutable, and it counts a failure from when its assembly started, which is slightly conservative. The better fix is to keep a stable failure timestamp (a `failedAt` field written with `status: 'failed'`, or a cleanup update that does not touch `updated_at`). Add a test with a failed row cleaned up later, and assert that both the cutoff and the displayed time use the failure time.

## Non-blocking Findings

### [ux] A row labeled `hold-for-uat` in a multi-row queue loses the skipped-UAT warning — `MergeTrainView.tsx:498`
- Severity: ~
- Classification: implementation defect (copy); in_pr_scope.
- `queueEntryForProject` (`merge-train.ts`) resolves an issue's own label only when the queue holds exactly one row. With two or more rows, `holdsForUat` is the project default. `onMergeRow` passes that section value to `mergeRowConfirmCopy`, which drops the "this merge skips batch testing" note when the value is `false`.
- Impact: in an auto-merge project with two or more ready rows and no tested batch (the batch is assembling or it failed), a row the operator labeled `hold-for-uat` merges after a confirm that does not say it skips UAT. The merge gate does not stop it. `evaluateIssueMergeGate` resolves the UAT requirement only when a failed UAT verdict exists on the head, so a held feature with no verdict merges. This is bounded, because the operator authored the label and clicks Merge on purpose. The old escape hatch always showed a "bypasses batch testing" warning.
- Fix: return each item's effective hold (`issueHoldsForUat`) on queue items, or always show the note unless the hold is known to be false for that row. Add a test with a held row in a mixed multi-row queue.

### [ux] The 6-hour window costs at most three failed assemblies per window
- Severity: ?
- This is by design (FR-1), and the docs and the log line say so. I note it only as a hypothesis to watch: a deterministic failure now uses three worktrees every 6 hours instead of stopping for good.

Blocking finding 1 and the non-blocking UAT-warning finding are here. |

### Dimensions
- **Correctness:** two FR-4 defects (blocking) and one copy defect (advisory). The route and the streak loop are otherwise correct.
- **Security:** no new trust boundary. `issueId` only selects an entry from the server-computed ready set and then passes the existing eligibility and merge gate. The route keeps the existing dashboard mutation auth and JSON-object checks. No findings.
- **Performance:** none. The route adds one linear `find` over the ready set. The view adds O(generations) derivations per section.
- **Requirements/UX:** see the matrix below. The NonGoals hold: `auto-merge-executor.ts`, `merge-strike.ts` and `pr-facts.ts` are unchanged, no new HTTP route was added, and the single-feature rule is unchanged.

### Requirement / AC matrix
| Item | Status | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FR-1: failures older than 6 hours stop counting; force bypasses | Partially met | The loop and the tests pass. The age is measured from `updatedAt`, which is the cleanup time (blocking finding 2). |
| FR-2: `merge-next` accepts `issueId`, 409 outside the ready set, 400 when malformed | Met | Route code and route tests pass (69/69 with the reconciler file). |
| FR-3: per-row Merge when no tested batch exists; Merge batch stays primary with the escape hatch | Met (with an advisory) | View code and view tests. CI has not run them yet. Missing UAT note for multi-row held rows (non-blocking). |
| FR-4: name the failure and its time; offer Retry; never promise a batch it will not build | Unmet | Blocking findings 1 and 2. |
| FR-5: docs | Met | `docs/MERGE-WORKFLOW.md` has the "Merging from the Flywheel UAT card" section. |
| AC: reconciler tests (old failures assemble, failures in the window block) | Met | `uat-reconciler.test.ts` passed locally. |
| AC: route tests (issueId merges only that feature, 409 outside) | Met | `merge-train.test.ts` passed locally. |
| AC: view tests (row buttons and body, failure copy, retry POST, rows hidden with a batch) | Unverified | The tests exist. They could not run locally (see Verification), and the CI test shards are pending. |
| AC: docs section | Met | Present. |
| Issue AC: batch assembles live after deploy | Unverified | Needs a deploy. The PR names it as an operator check. |

This is a workspace environment problem, and I did not touch node_modules. The result is unverified.

- I did not run the full suite, per the role.

## Scope Note
The plan critique raised all three findings before review as `blocks-the-design`, and none of them was addressed. The two blocking fixes are small: the Retry condition, and `createdAt` or a stable `failedAt` field, each with one test. The advisory needs each row's effective hold on the queue item.
